AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE INTERVAL SCHEDULE - MODEL FB-220 TURBOPROP

SECTION 1: SCHEDULED INSPECTIONS

The Main Landing Gear Wheel Bearing shall be inspected and repacked every 4,000 flight hours or 24 months, whichever comes first. The Nose Gear Strut requires servicing every 2,500 flight hours or 18 months, whichever comes first. The Brake Wear Pin must be visually checked every 400 flight hours or 6 months, whichever comes first.

The Engine Oil Filter shall be replaced every 300 flight hours or 400 cycles, whichever comes first. The Cabin Air Filter is replaced every 1,200 flight hours or 12 months, whichever comes first. The Fuel Boost Pump receives an operational check every 800 flight hours or 6 months, whichever comes first.

SECTION 2: TORQUE VALUES

The Cargo Door Actuator attachment bolts shall be torqued to 450 inch-pounds (50.8 newton-metres). The Engine Fan Blade root fasteners shall be torqued to 850 inch-pounds (96.0 newton-metres). The Wheel Well Fire Detection Loop mounting clamps shall be torqued to 35 inch-pounds (4.0 newton-metres).

SECTION 3: FLUID CAPACITIES

The Hydraulic Reservoir holds a fluid capacity of 4.5 US gallons. The Engine Oil Filter system, including sump, holds a fluid capacity of 14 quarts.

SECTION 4: MINIMUM EQUIPMENT LIST DISPATCH TIMES

With the Standby Attitude Indicator inoperative, the aircraft may be dispatched for a maximum of 10 days before repair is required. With the Weather Radar Antenna Drive Motor inoperative, the aircraft may be dispatched for a maximum of 3 days before repair is required. With the APU Fire Bottle inoperative, the aircraft may be dispatched for a maximum of 1 day before repair is required.

SECTION 5: LIFE-LIMITED PARTS

The Engine Fan Blade has a life limit of 22,000 cycles. The Emergency Locator Transmitter Battery has a life limit of 60 months from the date of manufacture. The Life Raft has a life limit of 72 months from the date of manufacture, subject to inspection.
